changes.evidence: 01_brand_front_or_keg_collar.jpg, lower-left text block: 'Bottled by TUBES USA, Inc. | Napa ... | Wine by Kendall-Jackson Vineyards & Winery, Santa Rosa, CA | PRODUCT OF USA'. Domestic California wine (registry origin CALIFORNIA, BW-CA permit); the rule says country_of_origin_text is for imports only, null for domestic. The words are printed, so only the field-rule makes this a change.

unsure.note: 02_back.jpg top line prints 'FINISHED AND BOTTLED IN THE UNITED STATES'. Product is domestic (DSP-IL-58, origin ILLINOIS), so by the imports-only rule this would be null; but it is a Caribbean rum finished in the US, so the statement is origin-related. Same policy question as 24039001000605; owner to decide.
Sheet says 'unclear'. On 02_back.jpg the heading is heavy bold and the body is a condensed regular weight; 'no' looks right, but the condensed font is dark so 'unclear' is defensible.

Sheet 'BELGIAN-STYLE WHEAT ALE' is printed on the front (under BELGIAN WHITE) and is fine. The side panel of 01_brand_front_or_keg_collar.jpg also prints the fuller statement 'BELGIAN-STYLE WHEAT ALE BREWED WITH CORIANDER & ORANGE PEEL' (registry: flavored malt beverage specialty). Keep unless the owner wants the full statement of composition. 'PUERTO RICO' at top right is a market mark, not origin; null is correct.
Sheet 'STOUT'. Front prints 'FOREIGN EXTRA' / 'STOUT' on two lines; back text says 'GUINNESS FOREIGN EXTRA STOUT'. STOUT is fine; 'FOREIGN EXTRA STOUT' would also be fair. No change proposed.
Sheet uses the US sticker (03_other.png: '40 ALC/VOL (80 PROOF) | 750 ML'), which is printed and correct. The original label (01) also prints '40% vol.' and '75 cl'. No change; noting both exist.
